name: pwm_fpga_demo
description: Single-clock FPGA-friendly PWM LED demo for board prototyping. The design generates a visible breathing/fading effect on one LED by using an internal slow counter to derive a timing enable, an 8-bit PWM counter, an 8-bit duty-cycle register, and a direction bit that ramps duty cycle up and down continuously. Intended for synthesizable open-source Lattice FPGA flows including lint, Yosys, nextpnr, timing review, and bitstream handoff.

fixed_assumptions: A single board clock input named clk is used.
No external reset port is required; internal state initializes in a safe demo state via power-up/resettable synthesis intent as supported by the target FPGA flow.
The LED pin is assumed to be active-high unless the board-specific constraint file indicates otherwise; starter constraints must be reviewed before physical hardware programming.
The breathing rate should be slow enough for visible human perception and should rely on a counter-derived update enable rather than clock division primitives.

functionality: Implement a minimalist, synthesizable PWM LED breathing demo. Internally maintain a slow free-running counter to create a low-rate update tick. Use an 8-bit PWM counter that continuously increments each clock to compare against an 8-bit duty-cycle register. When pwm_counter is less than duty_cycle, drive the LED on; otherwise drive it off. At each slow update tick, adjust the duty-cycle register by one count in the current direction. When the duty-cycle register reaches its maximum value, reverse direction and decrement on subsequent update ticks; when it reaches its minimum value, reverse direction and increment on subsequent update ticks. The result is a repeating fade-in/fade-out brightness pattern visible on the LED. The RTL must be fully synthesizable and avoid ASIC-only features, delays, real-number types, DPI, memories, vendor primitives, and testbench-only constructs.
responsibilities: Accept the single board clock input clk.
Generate an internal slow timing event from a counter to control the breathing rate.
Maintain an 8-bit PWM counter for brightness modulation.
Maintain an 8-bit duty-cycle register that is slowly incremented and decremented.
Maintain a direction bit that toggles at the duty-cycle endpoints.
Drive led with the PWM comparison result to produce visible brightness modulation.
Remain compatible with Lattice FPGA open-source synthesis and place-and-route flows.
must_not_drive: Any board-specific constraint files; those are generated separately after board selection.
Any external reset signal, since none is part of the requested interface.
Any vendor-specific primitive or macro outputs.
reset_behavior: With no external reset port, the design shall rely on FPGA-compatible initialization semantics or synchronous/implicit power-up initialization for all registers to a known safe demo state: duty cycle starts near minimum brightness or at a defined low value, the direction bit is set to count upward, the PWM counter starts at zero, and the slow counter starts at zero. If the target synthesis flow requires explicit initial values for deterministic startup, those values shall be static, synthesizable, and compatible with the target FPGA family.
behavior_rules: The top module name must be pwm_fpga_demo exactly.
The design must use only one input clock named clk and one output named led.
The PWM counter must be 8 bits wide.
The duty-cycle register must be 8 bits wide.
The direction control must be a single bit.
The slow counter must be large enough to create a human-visible breathing rate; its exact width may be chosen to suit the target clock frequency while remaining synthesizable.
The LED output shall be a combinational or registered function of the PWM comparison between the 8-bit PWM counter and the 8-bit duty-cycle register.
The duty cycle shall increment by one on each slow update tick while direction indicates up-counting, and decrement by one while direction indicates down-counting.
The direction bit shall invert only when the duty cycle reaches its minimum or maximum boundary.
The counter-based breathing update rate shall be much slower than the PWM carrier rate so the fade is smooth and visible.
No memories, no testbench logic, no delays, and no non-synthesizable system tasks shall be used in the top module.
The generated RTL shall be suitable for lint, Yosys synthesis, nextpnr place-and-route, timing review, and bitstream handoff.
Board-specific starter pin constraints shall be generated after board selection and must be reviewed before programming hardware.
Use PCF constraints for iCE40 targets and LPF constraints for ECP5 targets.
